method: Official websites and public GitHub repository pages. Star counts are rounded observations, not exact API totals. Effort and caveats are implementation judgments.

sources.name: React Bits
sources.effort: Low for CSS; medium/high for WebGL
sources.caveat: Commons Clause adds restrictions; preserve license and inspect component dependencies. WebGL effects need mobile performance checks.

sources.name: Magic UI
sources.license: MIT for public repo; Pro separate
sources.caveat: Strong marketing effects; combine selectively with quieter product controls.

sources.name: Paper Shaders
sources.caveat: README explicitly asks to pin dependency: breaking changes can occur under 0.0.x versions. Keep LICENSE/NOTICE when redistributing library code.

sources.name: Drei / React Three Fiber
sources.caveat: 3D foundation rather than drop-in DOM UI. Requires GPU, camera/light setup, asset work and fallback.

sources.name: tsParticles
sources.framework: Vanilla plus React/Vue/Svelte/Angular and other adapters
sources.caveat: Load only required engine/plugins and reduce particle density on mobile.

sources.name: NES.css
sources.caveat: Provides components rather than page layout. Retro typography can reduce density/readability.

sources.name: 98.css
sources.caveat: CSS only: draggable windows and desktop behavior require separate JS.

sources.name: Neobrutalism Components
sources.caveat: Opinionated thick borders and shadows can overwhelm dense dashboards.

sources.name: shadcn/ui
sources.caveat: Excellent functional baseline but visual distinction needs your own tokens. Accessibility still depends on composition.

sources.name: daisyUI
sources.license: MIT public library; paid products separate
sources.caveat: CSS classes provide styling; complex widget behavior still needs application code.

sources.name: Vaul
sources.caveat: A focused drawer primitive; validate touch, scrolling, focus, and background scaling in your actual app.

sources.name: Rough.js
sources.caveat: Drawing engine rather than accessible controls. Use semantic HTML for interaction and SVG for decorative treatment.

sources.name: Anime.js
sources.framework: Vanilla JS; adaptable to any frontend
sources.caveat: Animation engine requires composing your own components and cleaning up animations in framework lifecycles.

sources.name: css-doodle
sources.license: MIT component; public doodles MIT per current service terms
sources.caveat: Large DOM grids can be expensive. Good for decorative surfaces, not functional widget primitives.

sources.name: Open Props
sources.license: License file exists; exact terms not verified in this pass
sources.caveat: Token foundation rather than a component collection.

sources.name: Uiverse
sources.license: Official site states all UI elements MIT
sources.caveat: Community quality varies. Check each snippet's semantics, keyboard behavior and CSS isolation.

sources.name: Haikei
sources.license: Asset export rights not independently verified
sources.caveat: Exported static assets, not animated interactive components.

sources.name: shadcn-svelte
sources.caveat: Community-led port; use when Svelte is your implementation target.

sources.name: Vanta.js
sources.framework: Vanilla JS; Three.js or p5.js; framework adapters by lifecycle integration
sources.caveat: Official site recommends at most one or two instances on a page, warns of slow WebGL on older devices and mobile incompatibility, and requires a fallback. This gallery uses actual Vanta with its documented older Three.js version isolated from modern Three.js demos.

sources.name: Souradip
sources.license: Inspiration only; original site footage, artwork and code are not licensed for redistribution
sources.framework: Observed: HTML chapter cards with two muted video elements; exact underlying stack not confirmed
sources.bestFor: Immersive portfolio storytelling with a distinctive crafted visual world
sources.caveat: Browser inspection found two video elements and no canvas. Scroll/click triggers cinematic chapter changes. Footage and illustration production, media loading, navigation and reduced motion are major implementation concerns. The local demo uses original real-time Three.js geometry, not the source’s videos or assets.
sources.visualInspection: Observed chapters 01 and 02, wheel/click transitions, camera travel and fading content cards; native browser DOM contained two muted video elements and zero canvases.

sources.name: Tabler Icons
sources.framework: Plain SVG plus React, Vue, Svelte, Angular and other official packages
sources.bestFor: Consistent icons for navigation, actions, dashboards and product controls
sources.caveat: Use accessible labels on icon-only buttons; decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology. Ship the icons you use instead of bundling the complete collection in a product.

sources.name: Lando Norris
sources.license: Inspiration only; source models, photography, branding and code are not licensed for reuse
sources.framework: Observed WebGL/canvas helmet interaction and Webflow-style DOM; exact animation implementation not confirmed
sources.bestFor: A distinctive interactive 3D product or personality hero
sources.caveat: Requires model/material production, hit testing or a reveal mask, pointer/touch handling, reduced motion and performance fallbacks. The local study uses original procedural geometry and a screen-space reveal shader.
sources.install: No component package; this is a bespoke website reference
sources.visualInspection: Observed ghost/wireframe helmet, coloured helmet patches revealed by pointer movement, pointer-dependent orientation, and tap-to-lock/back-to-scroll control. Tested default and desktop widths. Rendered DOM contained canvases and no videos.

excludedOrDeferred.name: Inspira UI
excludedOrDeferred.reason: Official site fetch returned very little content and GitHub repo URL was unavailable; do not imply its licensing or specific components were verified.

excludedOrDeferred.name: particles.js
excludedOrDeferred.reason: Original engine exists; tsParticles offers broader modern adapters and effect presets for this directory.

excludedOrDeferred.name: Codrops
excludedOrDeferred.reason: Useful experimental inspiration; verify license and dependencies per demo repository, not as a blanket library license.
